steps.title: Confirm Yukon Business Nominee eligibility
steps.description: Score at least 65 points, have high-school education, at least three years of entrepreneurial or management experience and five years of relevant work experience. You need at least $500,000 net worth and $300,000 liquid assets verified by a Yukon accounting firm, and must intend to live in Yukon.

requiredDocuments.title: Education, experience, net-worth and liquid-asset evidence

preparationChecklist.text: Read the current official instructions for this stage.
Keep copies of submissions, confirmations and messages.

commonMistakes: Using outdated requirements or forms.
Missing a deadline or failing to report a material change.

steps.title: Develop an eligible Yukon business concept
steps.description: Plan a new or purchased Yukon business that you have not started or bought before program acceptance. You must hold a TEER 0 or 1 role and show at least $300,000 in qualifying capital investment during the first two years.

requiredDocuments.title: Yukon business concept and investment plan

steps.title: Prepare language and assessment-grid evidence
steps.description: Meet the current language requirement and document every claim on the assessment grid. The official application page currently specifies IELTS level 6 or TEF Canada level 4 and requires at least 65 points.

steps.title: Submit the original Yukon business application
steps.description: Complete and submit the signed YBNP application using the official delivery instructions. Initial review determines whether eligibility, points and the business concept allow entry to the candidate pool.

steps.title: Enter the six-month candidate pool
steps.description: Eligible applications with at least 65 points and an approved concept enter a potential-candidate pool for six months. Meeting the threshold does not guarantee selection.

steps.description: If selected from the pool, submit the records requested to verify application claims, lawful source of funds and the business plan.

steps.title: Complete the exploratory visit and interview
steps.description: Travel to Yukon when invited, investigate the market and attend the in-person interview. Be ready to explain the concept, investment, management role and settlement plan.

steps.title: Receive conditional business approval
steps.description: If approved after interview, review the territorial conditions and obtain Yukon's support for a two-year federal work permit. This is not yet the permanent residence nomination.

steps.description: Apply to IRCC with Yukon's support. IRCC decides the work permit. Follow the arrival and reporting instructions after approval.

steps.title: Establish and actively operate the Yukon business
steps.description: Settle in Yukon with accompanying family, make the approved capital investment, establish or purchase the business and actively manage it during the two-year work-permit period.

steps.title: Receive the Yukon business nomination
steps.description: If Yukon confirms the requirements were met, it issues the nomination for permanent residence. Nomination is not federal permanent resident status.
